title: Chanta Launches Noro-Noro Puku-Puku Manga
content:
Manga creator Chanta launched a new manga titled Noro-Noro Puku-Puku in Shueisha 's Shonen Jump+ manga service on Monday. The manga is available in English on Shueisha 's MANGA Plus service. MANGA Plus describes the manga:

An exceptionally cursed shrine maiden, Suzu, incurs the divine punishment of the gods one day... And her curse? To exorcise 108 curses with the help of Puku, the black cat possessing her head! Chanta of "Sachi's Records 〜Sachi's Book of Revelation〜" presents this jaw-dropping absurdist exorcist comedy!

Chanta launched the Sachi's Records: Sachi's Book of Revelation ( Sachi-roku: Sachi no Mokushiroku ) manga in Shueisha 's Shonen Jump+ website in July 2023, and ended it in April 2025. Shueisha published the manga's fifth and final compiled book volume in July 2025. Shueisha 's MANGA Plus service released the manga in English.
author: ANN

title: Naoki Shigeno to End Sanada Damashii Manga in 6th Volume
content:
Hakusensha is listing the sixth volume of Naoki Shigeno 's Sanada Damashii manga series as the final volume. The volume will ship on November 27.

The series is a four-panel comic depicting the activities of the Sanada clan in the Sengoku period.

Shigeno launched the series on Hakusensha 's Young Animal Densi platform in 2015, where it ran until 2017. It later switched to Hakusensha 's Manga Park platform. Hakusensha shipped the fifth compiled book volume in April 2025.

Shigeno launched the Nobunaga no Shinobi ( Ninja Girl & Samurai Master ) manga in Hakusensha 's Young Animal magazine in 2008, and ended it on July 25, 2025. Hakusensha published the manga's first volume in 2009. Hakusensha published the three-volume spinoff manga titled Nobunaga no Shinobi Gaiden: Owari Tōitsu-ki (Nobunaga's Shinobi - Chronicle of Owari's Unification) from 2014 to 2017. The original manga inspired a television anime in 2016. The anime's 26-episode second season premiered in 2017, and the third season premiered in 2018. Crunchyroll streamed all three seasons of the anime.

title: Nijū-Mensō no Musume's Shinji Ohara Launches New Manga
content:
Shinji Ohara launched a new manga titled Moto-Shojo Tantei, Yamada Chizuko: Saigo no Jiken kara Sūjūnengo (Former Girl-Detective, Chizuko Yamada: A Few Decades After the Final Case) on Shogakukan 's Yawaraka Spirits platform on September 30.

The story follows Kazuo Sasauchi, a young man who moves to Osaka to attend college and therefore moves into in an old western-styled house there. He meets the house's owner who is his great-aunt: the kimono-wearing, cigarette-smoking Chizuko Yamada. She is a former girl-detective whose past returns to haunt her.

Ohara ended the first Chiko, Heiress of the Phantom Thief ( Nijū-Mensō no Musume ) manga in 2007 after five years and eight volumes. Ohara launched the spinoff series Nijū-Mensō no Musume : Utsushiyo Yoru in Media Factory 's Monthly Comic Flapper in October 2007. Kadokawa published the 11th and final volume in 2014. The stories are loosely based on the Kaijin Nijū-Mensō (The Fiend with 20 Faces) novels by the famed suspense and detective novelist, Ranpo Edogawa. The first manga series inspired a television anime in April 2008.

title: K Manga Offers Adachitoka's The Wolf at Memory's End Manga in English
content:
K MANGA announced on Saturday that it will release Adachitoka 's The Wolf at Memory's End ( Yadoya no Oinu-sama ) manga in English on October 5.

Adachitoka is launching the manga in Kodansha 's Monthly Shonen Magazine on October 6.

The story follows Kasumi Kuromine, a junior high school girl who resides in the countryside. One day, an accident happens during a school field trip, and she falls down the mountainside.

Adachitoka launched the Noragami: Stray God manga in Monthly Shonen Magazine in 2010, and ended the series in January 2024. Kodansha shipped the 27th and final volume in February 2024. The manga inspired a 12-episode television anime series that premiered in January 2014. Funimation streamed the series as it aired and released it on home video. The anime's second season, titled Noragami Aragoto , debuted in October 2015, and Funimation also streamed that series as it aired and released it on home video.

Kodansha released the first volume of Noragami: Stray Stories in Japan in November 2013. BONES adapted one of the stories from the manga as an original anime DVD that shipped with the 15th volume of the manga in Japan.

title: Chained Soldier Manga Goes on Hiatus Due to Artist Yōhei Takemura's Health
content:
Shueisha 's Shonen Jump+ manga website announced on Saturday that writer Takahiro and artist Yōhei Takemura 's Chained Soldier ( Mato Seihei no Slave or literally, Slave of the Magic Capital's Elite Troops) manga will go on hiatus due to artist Takemura's poor health. In a statement, Takemura said that they injured their right wrist in June, specifically damage to the fibrocartilage. Takemura added that they have been drawing while wearing a brace, but drawing places a heavy strain on their wrist, causing pain and impeding recovery. Takemura added that full recovery requires a long period of time, and they have decided to stop working on the manga's drafts to allow their wrist to heal.

The editorial staff of Shonen Jump+ reported that the manga is scheduled to resume on November 14, but Takemura's recovery is top priority, and added that the manga's pace in the future will be determined in consultation with Takahiro and Takemura, and based on medical advice.

The battle fantasy is set in a world where a demonic gate has unleashed monsters known as Shūki. A special peach tree is able to give special powers, but only to women. The story begins when a down-on-his-luck boy named Yūki Wakura meets Uzen Kyōka, a girl who has gained the power of the peach, and is the captain of the 7th Anti-Demon Squad.

Takahiro ( Akame ga KILL! ) and Takemura ( Papa no Iu Koto o Kikinasai! manga) launched the manga on Shonen Jump+ manga website in January 2019. Yen Press publishes the manga in English.

The first season of the manga's anime adaptation premiered in Japan in January 2024. HIDIVE streamed the anime as it aired, and also streamed an English dub . The second season premiered on January 8. HIDIVE also streamed the second season as it aired, and also streamed an English dub . A third season is in the works.

title: BookWalker Adds 18 Ecomix Media Company Titles
content:
BookWalker also posted on Linkedin last week that "Premium" and "Early Access" creators on the North American webtoon platform Tapas , particularly those who are impacted by that platform's closure and are "seeking a stable, dedicated storefront to publish and monetize [their] series," can reach out to BookWalker . Tapas will end its service on March 31, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. PDT.

BookWalker added the following ongoing series:

• Don't Look for Me

• Falling

• Living with the Dangerous Beast

• The 100-Day Alpha Project

• The Duke Who Fell into Darkness Dotes on the Villainess

• To You Who Will Ruin Me

The service added the following completed series:

• All I Want is You

• Bring the Love

• Clean with Passion for Now

• Full Moon Alchemist

• Hard-Boiled Love

• Obscene Contract

• Royal Wedding

• The Bride of Darkness

• The First Night With the Duke

• The Maid and the Vampire

• The Villainess Behind the Mask

• Wife for 1000 Days

BookWalker launched a rebuilt website , apps, and a reader in March. The rebuilt system includes the previously announced Lightweight Content Protection (LCP) DRM system, which allows users to access purchases through LCP-compatible reading apps outside of BookWalker . All English-language manga and light novels moved to the new BookWalker website and app, while Japanese content will remain on the existing website and app.

BookWalker Global changed in ownership from BookWalker Co., Ltd. to M12 Media LLC (formerly J-Novel Club LLC) in March 2025. BookWalker Co., Ltd. and J-Novel Club /M12 Media LLC are both Kadokawa Group companies.

title: CloverWorks' Omnibus Anime Film Grotesqqque Streams New English-Subtitled Trailer
content:
Aniplex USA streamed a new English-subtitled trailer for Atsushi Nishigori 's original anime film Grotesqqque (previously titled Grotesque) on Sunday.

The film is an omnibus film of three stories with different worldviews.

Atsushi Nishigori ( The IDOLM@STER , DARLING in the FRANXX ) is directing the film, and is also writing the screenplay and designing the characters.

The band METALVERSE performs the opening theme song "Shoot Shoot Shoot." Haoto performs the ending theme song with lyrics by momosu momosu.

The film comes from JOEN , the company jointly established by Sony media subsidiary Aniplex , its CloverWorks animation studio, Production I.G sister company Wit Studio , and publisher Shueisha . CloverWorks producer Yūichi Fukushima and Wit Studio producer Tetsuya Nakatake are the representative directors of JOEN .

The film will open in Japan on November 6. The film had its world premiere at this year's Fantasia International Film Festival , which took place in Montreal from July 16-August 2.

The Japan Society will host the the U.S. premiere of the film in collaboration with CloverWorks and Aniplex of America in New York City on October 8. Director Nishigori will give a pre-screening introduction in-person at the event.

title: Black Clover Season 2’s Premiere Confirms the Disappointing Update Fans Feared
content:
After five years of silence, Black Clover has finally returned in all its glory, with improved animation and the adaptation of the important arcs of the series that fans have been waiting for since the anime came to an end. The series has emerged as one of the most important Shonen Jump series, with its original run carrying the legacy of what shonen anime has come to represent. In its first run, Black Clover delivered a total of 170 episodes, with the series only adapting up to Chapter 270 of the manga. It was able to do this thanks to Studio Pierrot providing plenty of anime-original content and extending certain scenes.

Studio Pierrot had done this with many of its shonen series previously as well, including major titles such as Naruto , Boruto , and Bleach . With Black Clover being one of the latest series to follow this approach, fans had expected the anime’s return with its second season to follow a similar format. However, the premiere episode of Black Clover Season 2 confirms that the series will be following a fast-paced narrative in its second season . The first episode seemingly adapts almost five chapters from the manga. This has more than confirmed that Black Clover will only be around for a short while, with only 25–30 episodes at most.

Black Clover Season 2 Won’t Be as Big as the First Season

In particular, the premiere episode of Black Clover Season 2 adapts Chapters 271 to 275, along with some pages, seemingly covering around 4.5 chapters per episode. Given that the manga’s pace for this arc continues this way, with more fast-paced action between the dialogue, it is highly likely that every episode of this season will adapt a similar number of chapters. If that is the case, the series could adapt the remaining chapters of the manga in just 25–30 episodes at most, seemingly concluding Black Clover ’s run within the next year. Another element is how Studio Pierrot treated another anime similarly when it returned to adapt its final arc.

It is none other than Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War , which is structured to adapt around 200 chapters in 50 episodes. The final arc of the series is fast-paced, without the anime-original elements seen in the original run. Studio Pierrot is clearly aiming for a similar pattern with Black Clover as well, and if that is true, then adapting the remaining 120 chapters could be done in only 25–30 episodes. Thanks to Bleach ’s final arc adaptation being split into different parts, Black Clover could follow a similar structure, with potentially only two cours. The first part of the second season, with around 13 episodes, a staple of seasonal anime, could adapt the entire Spade Kingdom arc from the manga, covering around 60 chapters.

After this, there could be a break for the anime, probably lasting 3–6 months, meaning the second and final part of Black Clover Season 2 could arrive in either Spring or Summer of next year, with another set of 13 episodes, concluding the series as well. In some ways, this decision is much better for the series, as it will help fans see the story as soon as possible without the slow-paced and filler episodes that many fans complained about. Yet, Black Clover abandoning this format is indeed disappointing, as it was one of the last series to adapt a shonen manga in such a way, and changing it confirms that Shonen Jump anime adaptations have evolved and that there may never be such an anime adaptation again in the future.

title: 3 Anime to Watch If You Miss Spy x Family
content:
WIT Studio and CloverWorks’ Spy x Family anime has emerged as one of the most iconic anime ever, and it is undoubtedly prominent thanks to its main character, Anya. The series blends the charm of family with the found family trope, with every member of the family harboring their own secrets. However, despite their secrets, they ultimately emerge as a family that fans have come to find charming and adorable.

Across its three seasons, the anime has provided the perfect blend of comedy and action, while its latest season has also proven that its foundation is built on darker elements than it implies. This is why finding an anime that can be this diverse is a difficult task. However, there are a few anime, particularly these three, that fans can pick up in Spy x Family ‘s absence.

3) Kotaro Lives Alone

Spy x Family ‘s most intriguing element is how Anya behaves so maturely despite being only 4-5 years old. This is what Kotaro Lives Alone also projects with its over-the-top trope, yet viewers can’t help but feel bad for Kotaro. As the title suggests, it features a 4-5-year-old boy named Kotaro, who has just moved into a new house and lives alone. Kotaro immediately reveals that his intention is to be a good neighbor and not bother others.

However, seeing a four-year-old living alone naturally prompts curiosity, and the neighbors start trying to show him love as they try to discover why Kotaro is living all alone. It has its own sort of found family trope that you wouldn’t expect in real life, but it is charming enough for you to start taking care of Kotaro. As the show progresses and it gradually reveals where Kotaro’s maturity stems from, it ends up providing a perfect explanation for Kotaro’s situation.

2) Buddy Daddies

Buddy Daddies is the anime that has been called the most like Spy x Family , and the reason is more than evident in its premise. However, the series also evolves into a thing of its own, yet it never loses the charm that made Spy x Family so appealing to fans. It features two assassins, Rei and Kazuki, who have just finished a mission, taking down a man. However, it turns out that this man is the father of a daughter who has just arrived in Tokyo.

The comical twist is that Miri has never seen her father, and thus, she ends up mistaking Kazuki for her father. Thus begins the journey of two male assassins taking in a daughter and becoming a cute found family that they never imagined, all while continuing to work as assassins. From action to comedy, it has all the elements of Spy x Family that you want and will undoubtedly help fill the void left by missing Spy x Family for a little while.

1) The Promised Neverland

For fans who have seen The Promised Neverland , it might be surprising to see it being compared to Spy x Family ; however, on a deeper level, there are quite a few similarities. In particular, it is about the dark elements surrounding the presence of the children, which one might find very surprising. While Spy x Family layered this foundation through its characters, with Anya and even Loid being victims of something much larger, The Promised Neverland takes a slightly different approach by showcasing the children as potential victims.

With the children being raised in an orphanage, it is initially implied that the series is about caregiving, but the dark reality of the children being raised to be eaten by monsters immediately hits very hard. Then begins the journey of the children using their wits, which they showcase in an epic way, providing a thrilling experience. It is a shame that the anime came to an end after just two seasons , never fully adapting the manga, but it is still a good show that fans can pick up, especially if they are missing Spy x Family and want a completely different experience.

With the children being raised in an orphanage, it is initially implied that the series is about caregiving, but the dark reality of the children being raised to be eaten by monsters immediately hits very hard. Then begins the journey of the children using their wits, which they showcase in an epic way, providing a thrilling experience. It is a shame that the anime came to an end after just two seasons , never fully adapting the manga, but it is still a good show that fans can pick up, especially if they are missing Spy x Family and want a completely different experience.

title: 20 Years Ago Today, Shonen Jump’s Darkest Anime Hero Changed the World Forever
content:
There’s no denying that Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump is the biggest manga magazine of all time, known for serializing several classics over the decades. Launched in 1968, the magazine eventually released fan-favorite series such as One Piece, Dragon Ball, Naruto , and many more acclaimed manga. The magazine has seen countless changes over the years, but the biggest one is the transition from long-running series to shorter stories. However, while that trend is new to fans in the 2010s and 2020s, Death Note is one of the shorter stories that somehow made its mark in the industry. Written by Tsugumi Ohba and illustrated by Takeshi Obata, the manga was serialized from 2003 to 2006.

It didn’t take long after the manga finale for Madhouse to release an anime adaptation, forever changing the Shonen industry. The anime premiered on October 4th, 2026, exactly two decades ago, but even after all this time, it wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say Death Note is one of the best series in anime history, filled with thriller, suspense, and supernatural elements. While the overall story in general is one-of-a-kind, what truly drew fans in is the exceptional main character, Light Yagami, who redefined what a Shonen protagonist could be .

Death Note Follows the Story of a Hero Turned Villain

The story centers around a genius high school student, Light Yagami, who becomes twisted after tasting the kind of power no mortal should’ve known about. While looking out from his classroom window, he saw a seemingly ordinary notebook falling from the sky. He later picked it up and realized it was a Death Note that claims to take the life of a person whose name is written on it if the user fulfills specific conditions, which are quite easy to follow. Although Light believes that the notebook is nothing but a prank, he still decides to experiment with it by using a felon’s name. He never expected he would succeed in killing the criminal, and it doesn’t take long for the teenager to form his own distorted sense of justice and decide to purge the world of all criminals by going on a murder spree.

Going under the alias “Kira,” Light evokes fear and unrest among the people until a mysterious detective known as L swears to stop Kira’s rampage. It also doesn’t help that the true owner of the notebook, Ryuk, a Shinigami, tries to use Light as a means of entertainment. What truly sets him apart is that he begins using the Death Note with a noble intention of ridding the world of criminals. However, the power he possessed in his hand was never something a mortal could handle. To be able to control life and death itself gave him the idea that the kind of a god complex that turned his sense of justice into something twisted.

Death Note Blurs the Line Between Good and Evil

In the process of getting rid of all the criminals in the world, Light never hesitated to use those around him . His goal was to create a peaceful utopia with no crime, but his dream was never fully realized since he became the one causing the chaos he once despised. He manipulated Kisa, who was clearly in love with him. Not to mention that he killed L and his father in hopes of hiding his identity. Light would also never hesitate to erase his memories and manipulate himself if the situation deemed it necessary. He wasn’t born evil, but the power he held turned him into something he couldn’t recognize anymore. In the end, he died a sad death at the hands of the Shinigami who had been using him all that time.

However, it’s not just Light, but the anime in general follows morally gray characters, which makes them all the more intriguing. Instead of painting everything as black or white, the story focuses on the complex characters and the nuance between every step they take. This haunting narrative doesn’t preach a simple lesson, but instead, it tests the viewers by showing a world where a person who lowers global crime rates forces the masses to question if the ends can ever justify the means. The story was never about justice but the lengths someone would go to justify their evil. Instead of a clash between good and evil, the story focuses on a battle of wits between morally gray characters where neither side is completely right or wrong.

Is Death Note one of your favorite anime as well? Let me know in the comments section what you like most about Light Yagami. Or you can just share your favorite Endgame moment to commemorate the anime’s anniversary.
